title: Coding Challenge 3: Encapsulation
description: Learn the principle of Encapsulation in Object-Oriented Programming. Encapsulation bundles data and methods together while hiding internal details and restricting direct access from outside components. In this challenge, create a SecretDiary class that protects a child's secrets from snooping parents! Use private class fields (with the '#' syntax) so that passcode and diary contents cannot be accessed directly, and can only be written or read by supplying the correct passcode.
requirements: The constructor should accept 'owner' and 'passcode' parameters
Use private class fields (#passcode and #content) to encapsulate private data
Implement a 'write(passcode, text)' method that updates #content and returns 'Entry added' if the passcode is correct, or returns 'Access denied' if incorrect
Implement a 'read(passcode)' method that returns #content if the passcode is correct, or returns 'Access denied' if incorrect
hints: Declare private fields at the top of the class body using the '#' prefix: #passcode; and #content = '';
Inside the constructor and methods, refer to private fields using 'this.#passcode' and 'this.#content'
Private fields cannot be accessed outside the class: diary.passcode and diary.content will be undefined
Compare the incoming passcode parameter with this.#passcode before allowing access
Return 'Access denied' when an incorrect passcode is provided

tests.name: SecretDiary class exists
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Alice', '1234'); return typeof d === 'object' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'SecretDiary is not a class' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: SecretDiary has public owner property
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Alice', '1234'); return d.owner === 'Alice' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'owner property is not set correctly' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Sensitive fields are encapsulated (not public properties)
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Bob', 'secret123'); if (d.passcode !== undefined) { return { success: false, message: 'passcode is exposed as a public property! Use a private field (#passcode)' }; } if (d.content !== undefined) { return { success: false, message: 'content is exposed as a public property! Use a private field (#content)' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: write() updates content with valid passcode
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Charlie', 'mySecretCode'); const writeRes = d.write('mySecretCode', 'Dear Diary, today was great!'); const readRes = d.read('mySecretCode'); return (writeRes === 'Entry added' && readRes === 'Dear Diary, today was great!') ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'write() or read() failed with valid passcode. Expected write to return "Entry added"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: read() denies access with incorrect passcode
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('David', 'key999'); d.write('key999', 'Top secret thoughts'); const readRes = d.read('wrongPasscode'); return readRes === 'Access denied' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Access denied", got "' + readRes + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: write() denies update with incorrect passcode
tests.test: function() { try { const d = new SecretDiary('Emma', 'pass123'); d.write('pass123', 'My secret'); const writeRes = d.write('parentSnooping', 'I found your diary!'); const readRes = d.read('pass123'); if (writeRes !== 'Access denied') { return { success: false, message: 'write() should return "Access denied" for incorrect passcode' }; } if (readRes !== 'My secret') { return { success: false, message: 'Diary content should not be changed by unauthorized access' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Uses private fields (#) for data encapsulation
tests.test: function() { try { const codeStr = SecretDiary.toString(); if (!codeStr.includes('#')) { return { success: false, message: 'SecretDiary must use private class fields (#) for encapsulation' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: Modern JavaScript private class fields used ✓
